accuracy.evidence: Checked for the metamorphosis lesson against Monarch Joint Venture 'Growth and development' (the larval cuticle stretches only a little so it is shed; five larval instars; wings, proboscis, eyes and legs grow from imaginal discs; the pupa grows wings and flight muscles and the gut changes from milkweed leaves to nectar, and it explicitly rejects the 'turns to liquid' picture, so the lesson says 'much of the body breaks down' and never 'soup'), University of Maryland Extension FS-1144 (egg about 3 to 5 days, larva 10 to 14 days, chrysalis 10 to 14 days; chewing mouthparts become a sipping tube), Kaleka et al. 2019 IntechOpen 'Larval development and molting' (grasshopper nymphs resemble adults, wing pads enlarge at each of 5 to 6 moults, three stages and no pupa), and the Royal Entomological Society and NHM life-cycle guides for which orders are complete (butterflies, beetles including ladybirds, flies, bees) and incomplete (grasshoppers, crickets, cockroaches, dragonflies). Adult insects not moulting, spiders as 8-legged non-insects whose young moult, and the dragonfly nymph caveat are stated. Every numeric item evaluated at its range corners (5-1 to 6-4 moults, 3+10+10 to 5+14+10 days, 4x1+3x1 to 4x3+3x3 stages, 5x5 to 5x10 days).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips: the hard skin stretches as the insect grows (prediction; feeding twice is refused with 'cannot stretch any more'), every insect has a pupa (prediction; a pupa dropped into the grasshopper cycle is refused; challenge 'Both of them'), a nymph looks nothing like the adult (challenge 'A worm with no legs'), a pupa is asleep (prediction; challenge 'Nothing: it is asleep'), a small butterfly is a baby that will grow (challenge and mastery m4), spiders are insects (spider card and challenge), and larva and adult eat the same food (prediction; nectar to the caterpillar is refused).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagmetam is about metamorphosis itself: a grasshopper nymph that must be fed and then dragged out of its exoskeleton five times, leaving a row of old skins as it grows and its wing pads enlarge into full wings; two side-by-side life cycles of 4 and 3 boxes with a pupa refused in the grasshopper lane; a clue-based sort into complete, incomplete or not an insect; a 10-day marker that rebuilds the inside of a chrysalis until the wing colours show and the butterfly emerges; and a food match contrasting larva and adult with nymph and adult. It is not 539 flagcycle (drawing one life cycle in order) or 712 flaglifest (animal life stages); the 6-token shingle gate reports no flag lab above 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: Learners discover each idea by acting: the skin outline turns red when they feed twice, so growth needs a moult; the grasshopper's cycle only has three boxes and refuses the pupa, so incomplete metamorphosis has no pupa; the clue text on each card (pupa or nymph) is what sorts it, so the rule is used, not memorised; the chrysalis visibly changes inside as days pass, so a pupa is not resting; and the food match shows larva and adult eating different food while nymph and adult share grass. Each finished task prints the rule and compares it with the prediction.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab then disproves: 'It stretches as it grows' (the skin goes tight and must be shed), 'Yes, all insects do' have a pupa (the grasshopper cycle refuses one), 'Yes, it is asleep' (the chrysalis rebuilds day by day), and 'Yes, the same' food (nectar and leaves are refused for the wrong eater). The reveal line names the right answer after the task.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven challenge questions; each wrong option has a named slip: no pupa in incomplete, only complete has a pupa, moulting is not about colour or cold, a nymph is not a worm, a pupa is not asleep or just growing, adults do not grow or moult, a spider is not an insect, and the caterpillar and butterfly do not share food. Clicked through all seven in a Playwright run; each shows its message and a Next button.

readability.evidence: Kid text FK grade 2.4 (family target 5.0) in short sentences, introducing moulting, larva, pupa and nymph with a plain meaning each time; adult text FK 9.5 (target 10) gives the curriculum link, the orders in each group, instars and moult counts, pupa length, imaginal discs and named mistakes. Canvas text is one heading per scene, stage cards with the everyday word in brackets (caterpillar, chrysalis), and short clue lines on the sort cards.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs: why insects moult; complete metamorphosis with its 4 stages; incomplete metamorphosis with its 3 stages; the food reason. Adult paragraphs: curriculum fit and which insects belong where; moulting, instars, pupa length and what happens inside; named mistakes and the dragonfly caveat; what the lab does. The content gate finds no filler phrase and no explanation above 12% overlap.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px phone screenshots in light and dark for every scene mid-task and finished: the nymph and leaf are large drag targets with old skins staggered in two rows above, the 4-box and 3-box life cycles fit the width with readable two-line labels, the seven clue cards sit in 2 columns above three bins, the day track spans the width with a 26 px marker and +1 and +3 day buttons, and the four food cards sit above a 2 by 2 grid of eaters with small drawings. Nothing is clipped.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: 'Feed it a leaf' and 'Moult: climb out of the old skin', '→ butterfly' and '→ grasshopper' per stage, 'Complete', 'Incomplete' and 'Not an insect' per animal (the aria-label includes the clue), '+1 day' announcing the day, and per-eater food buttons. The canvas aria-label carries the scene description and every piece of feedback; challenge feedback is a role=status live region; ✓ and ✗ mark state as well as colour; walk.cjs axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
